title: loop (while)
concept: The while statement repeats as long as the condition is true. This is suitable when the number of repetitions is not predetermined.

steps.title: Start main function
steps.explanation:
The main stack frame is created when the program starts.

The purpose of this lesson is to check the structure in which repetition proceeds and ends by checking the while condition and updating the value.

steps.title: Initial value settings
steps.explanation:
Prepare the variable to be used in while with `int n = 1;` outside the loop.

While requires you to write the initialization/update yourself, so it is important to have a clear starting value.

steps.title: while condition check (n = 1)
steps.explanation:
First checks if `n <= 4` is true, and if true, executes the body.

while is a condition-oriented loop, so if you omit the condition change code, it can easily result in an infinite loop.

steps.title: Round 1: Print current value
steps.explanation:
Print the current `n` value to check the iteration progress.

In while, this intermediate output is useful for debugging the flow.

steps.title: Round 1: Double n
steps.explanation:
`n = n * 2;` changes n from 1 to 2. This update code is required in while.

If there is no update, the condition will remain true, resulting in an infinite loop.

steps.title: Round 2: Condition test (n = 2)
steps.explanation:
After the update, `n=2`, so the condition is still true and we proceed to the next iteration.

The flow is `Check condition -> Execute body -> Update value` over and over again.

steps.title: Round 3: Condition test (n = 4)
steps.explanation:
Even in `n=4`, `n <= 4` is true, so the last body is executed one more time.

A subsequent update causes n to be 8 and terminates at the next check.

steps.title: End of iteration (n = 8)
steps.explanation:
When `n=8`, the while ends because `8 <= 4` is false.

When exiting a loop, the variable value may not be the "last executed value" but rather the "value that broke the condition."

steps.title: final n output
steps.explanation:
After the loop ends, the final value of `n` is output.

Note that the ending value may not be the last output value, but rather the value after breaking the condition.

steps.title: Program exit
steps.explanation:
Terminate the program normally with `return 0;`.

The key point of this example is that you have to manage the conditions and updates yourself in the while.

quiz.question: How does while (1) { ... } work?
quiz.explanation:
In C, 1 is true and 0 is false.

`while(1)` repeats infinitely because the condition is always true.
You must escape with a `break` statement.

misconceptions.wrong: A while statement is executed at least once even if the condition is false.
misconceptions.correct: while is never executed if the condition is false from the beginning.
misconceptions.why:
It is the do-while statement that guarantees execution at least once.
while checks the condition first before entering.

keyTakeaway: The while statement is 'when you don't know when it will end' — if the condition is true, keep repeating!
